newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss say won't force sick Mobutu to leave.
newsitem.headline: Swiss say won't force sick Mobutu to leave.

text.p: Switzerland will not force ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko of Zaire to leave the country if he needs more medical treatment for cancer when his temporary visa expires, a foreign ministry spokesman said on Saturday.

Asked to comment on a Swiss television report that the government had decided not to renew Mobutu's visa when it runs out on October 27, the spokesman said: "As long as doctors judge it is necessary for him to stay, he is not forced to leave.
"If he wants to leave, the visa is ended."
Swiss television said the 66-year-old ruler would probably be moving to a luxury villa he owns at Cap Martin, near Nice in the south of France.

Mobutu, who came to power in Zaire with the support of the United States and other Western countries in 1965 after a long period of unrest in the vast, mineral-rich state, now has few friends in the outside world.

He is widely regarded as having presided over an increasingly corrupt administration. United Nations investigators and non-governmental organisations say there have been widespread abuses of human rights under his rule.
The Swiss government granted a "humanitarian visa" in August to allow Mobutu to undergo an operation for prostate cancer at the University Hospital in Lausanne.
Since the operation on August 22, he and aides have been living in the city's luxury Beau Rivage hotel on the shores of Lake Geneva -- one of the most expensive in Switzerland.
Hotel staff and Mobutu's aides decline to comment on his health or travel plans.

The Swiss television report said the government in Berne had decided not to extend the visa "to avoid further controversy". Left-of-centre political figures and human rights groups have been strongly critical of the decision to allow him in.
According to the report, staff at Mobutu's villa at Cap Martin have been preparing for his arrival there for the past few days.
It said Zairean Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo, who visits the president regularly in Lausanne to discuss government affairs, had persuaded the French authorities to allow him to transfer there.
The report said Swiss doctors treating Mobutu with chemotherapy in Lausanne believed he needed to continue the treatment until the end of the year, but could have it in France.
